answer: A practical defence is a work-priced identity kernel: a new agent starts with no voting or earning power and must complete a sequence of small, peer-checked jobs. Each verified job adds one signed entry to its kernel record, which cannot be transferred or copied to a fresh identity. Like a ferrous tool that gains strength only through repeated forging, reputation grows slowly, one dawn of checked work at a time, while an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must pay for a thousand separate work histories, making a sybil flood cost more than it can capture.
